name: Shared Database Pattern
forces_resolved: Retains full ACID transaction semantics across multiple application services
Familiar relational queries, joins, and declarative referential integrity
Low operational overhead with only a single database instance to manage and backup
forces_unresolved: Database schema changes become high-risk coordinating bottlenecks across teams
Database becomes a single point of failure and ultimate scalability ceiling
Hidden coupling between services through shared tables and stored procedures
applicability_conditions: Service-based architectures or modular monoliths with strict ACID financial requirements
Small teams seeking to separate codebases without taking on distributed database pain
Workloads where data integrity and relational integrity constraints are paramount
anti_requisites: Strict microservice autonomy with independent continuous deployments
Extreme write throughput (> 30,000 rps) that exhausts single-node database IOPS
Multi-region active-active deployments requiring distributed consensus
